mainTopic: The source for stoning a מכשף, the levels of forbidden and permitted magic, and stories about sorcery and the plagues of מצרים.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about how a מכשף (sorcerer) is executed. רבי עקיבא finishes rejecting the sword opinion. בן עזאי learns סקילה from the verse placed right next to the מכשפה verse. רבי יהודה learns it from אוב and ידעוני, which the Torah singled out from the group of sorcerers. When the גמרא challenges רבי יהודה with the rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, רבי זכריה answers that רבי יהודה holds such verses do teach. The גמרא then turns to teachings about sorcery: רבי יוחנן explains the name כשפים, and רבי חנינא says sorcery cannot touch a person of great merit. אביי tells demon-work apart from sorcery. He also divides magic into three levels like שבת: real magic gets סקילה, illusion is פטור אבל אסור, and creating through הלכות יצירה is fully permitted. Stories follow about tricks, spells and the limits of demons. Then comes a dispute about the plague of frogs. Finally the גמרא returns to רבי עקיבא's statement in the משנה.

steps.title: End of רבי עקיבא's rejection: gentiles have only one death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The last words of רבי עקיבא's reply to רבי יוסי הגלילי: gentiles have only one kind of death penalty, so we cannot learn the Jewish law of מכשף from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...only one kind of death.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish רבי עקיבא's answer from the end of the ברייתא's argument. He is pushing away רבי יוסי הגלילי's proof that a מכשף is killed by the sword.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי learned the punishment of a מכשף from a verse about non-Jews, and non-Jews are killed by the sword. רבי עקיבא answers that Jews have many kinds of death penalty while non-Jews have only one, so you cannot learn a Jewish case from them. That knocks out the sword proof and keeps רבי עקיבא's own proof for סקילה standing; the ברייתא then brings other sources for סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: One kind of death penalty, the single punishment that applies to non-Jews

phrases.english: ...one kind of death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מיתה אחת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי עקיבא's rebuttal from the previous part of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוסי הגלילי's גזירה שוה that would make a מכשף punished by the sword.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He compares Jews, who have many death penalties, to non-Jews, who have only one.

steps.title: בן עזאי learns stoning from the verse placed next to it
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי says the verse about a מכשפה sits right next to the verse about lying with an animal, and since that sin gets סקילה, so does a מכשף.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: The Torah says 'You shall not let a witch live,' and right after it says 'Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.' The Torah put them side by side to teach that, just as one who lies with an animal is stoned, a sorcerer is also stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a new opinion. בן עזאי offers a different proof that a מכשף gets סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי uses the idea of סמוכים: two topics placed next to each other in the Torah share a law. Lying with an animal is punished by סקילה, so the verse just before it, about a מכשפה, gets סקילה too.

keyTerms.meaning: A witch, someone who does sorcery
One who lies with an animal
The Torah placed this topic right next to that one
Stoning, one of the four death penalties of בית דין

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
It is stated: 'You shall not let a witch live,'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:17

phrases.aramaic: וְנֶאֱמַר ״כׇּל שֹׁכֵב עִם בְּהֵמָה מוֹת יוּמָת״.
phrases.english: and it is stated: 'Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:18, the very next verse.

phrases.english: The Torah placed this topic next to that one,
to teach: just as one who lies with an animal is stoned,
so too a sorcerer is stoned.

steps.triggerLanguage: בן עזאי אומר נאמר מכשפה לא תחיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a further, independent source for סקילה, alongside רבי עקיבא's גזירה שוה, after the sword opinion was rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מכשף is killed by סקילה, learned because the verse sits next to the verse about lying with an animal.

steps.title: רבי יהודה rejects learning stoning just from verses placed side by side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה objects: can we give someone the harshest death penalty only because two verses sit next to each other?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Just because the Torah put this topic next to that one, should we take this person out to be stoned?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה pushes back against בן עזאי's proof. He thinks סמוכים is too weak a reason to sentence someone to סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the method, not on the result. רבי יהודה also holds that a מכשף gets סקילה. He just will not rely on two verses being next to each other for something as serious as stoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really because...? A way of saying a reason is too weak
We will take out, meaning take him out to be executed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
And just because the Torah placed this topic next to that one,
shall we take this person out to be stoned?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לו רבי יהודה וכי מפני שסמכו ענין לו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks בן עזאי's proof from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from סמוכים. The ruling of סקילה itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Placing verses side by side is not strong enough to decide on the severe penalty of סקילה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's own source: אוב and ידעוני were singled out to teach about all sorcerers
steps.stepSummary: אוב and ידעוני are types of sorcery that the Torah took out of the general group and gave סקילה. This teaches that every מכשף gets סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the necromancer (אוב) and the sorcerer (ידעוני) were part of the general group of sorcerers. Why did the Torah mention them separately? To compare the rest to them and tell you: just as אוב and ידעוני are stoned, so too every sorcerer is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting בן עזאי's proof, רבי יהודה gives his own proof that a מכשף gets סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אוב and ידעוני are really kinds of sorcery, yet the Torah gives them their own verse with סקילה. רבי יהודה reads this as a model for the whole group: whatever applies to them applies to every מכשף. The ruling is the same as בן עזאי's, but the source is different.

keyTerms.meaning: A necromancer, who raises up the dead to speak
A type of sorcerer who uses a special bone in his mouth
They were included in the general group
So why were they singled out?
To compare one case to another so they share the same law

phrases.english: Rather, a necromancer and a sorcerer
were included in the general group of sorcerers,
so why were they singled out?
phrases.notes: The Torah gives them their own verse with סקילה, in ויקרא 20:27.

phrases.english: To compare the others to them and tell you:
just as a necromancer and a sorcerer are stoned,
so too a sorcerer is stoned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אוב וידעוני בכלל מכשפים היו ולמה יצאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in step 3 with רבי יהודה's own source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מכשף is killed by סקילה, learned from אוב and ידעוני, which were singled out from the group of sorcerers.
steps.whatToRemember: Both בן עזאי and רבי יהודה agree that a מכשף gets סקילה. They argue only about where we learn it from: verses placed next to each other, or the singling out of אוב and ידעוני.

steps.title: Challenge: אוב and ידעוני are two verses teaching the same thing, which cannot teach about others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: אוב and ידעוני should count as שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, and such verses do not teach about other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה as well, let אוב and ידעוני be two verses that teach the same thing, and any two verses that teach the same thing do not teach about other cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רבי יהודה's proof using a known rule about how we learn from verses. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah gives the same law to two separate cases, that suggests the law applies only to them. Otherwise one example would have been enough. Since the Torah mentioned both אוב and ידעוני, maybe they are the exceptions and not a model for every מכשף.

keyTerms.meaning: According to רבי יהודה too
Let them be, meaning let them count as
Two verses that teach the same law
They do not teach about other cases

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'too' (נמי) does not mean רבי יהודה made this mistake along with someone else. The גמרא is saying: even with רבי יהודה's better-sounding source, there is still a problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד is a basic tool used all over ש״ס. It decides when a law stays limited to the cases the Torah names and when it spreads to similar cases.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda as well,
let the necromancer and the sorcerer be
two verses that come as one,
phrases.notes: Two verses that teach the same law, here סקילה, for two different cases.

phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one
do not teach about other cases!

steps.triggerLanguage: לרבי יהודה נמי ליהוו אוב וידעוני שני כתובים הבאים כאחד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof רבי יהודה offered in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's proof that every מכשף gets סקילה, learned from אוב and ידעוני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the Torah gives two separate examples with the same law, the rule שני כתובים הבאים כאחד אין מלמדין says that law stays limited to those two cases. So it cannot be extended to all sorcerers.

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds that two parallel verses do teach
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכריה answers the challenge. רבי יהודה holds the view that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד מלמדין, so he can learn every מכשף from אוב and ידעוני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rabbi Zekharya says: This shows that רבי יהודה holds that two verses that come as one do teach about other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זכריה answers the question from the last step. He says רבי יהודה simply holds a different rule about parallel verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that two verses teaching the same thing (אוב and ידעוני) cannot teach about other cases. רבי זכריה says רבי יהודה does not accept that rule. In his view such verses DO teach, so his לימוד from אוב and ידעוני to every מכשף works.

keyTerms.meaning: This means / this shows (a conclusion drawn from what was just said)
He holds (this is his opinion)
Two verses that come as one: two separate verses that teach the same law
They teach (about other cases too)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's view stands because he holds that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד מלמדין. So for him every מכשף gets סקילה, learned from אוב and ידעוני.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זכריה is not saying the challenge was wrong about the general rule. He is saying רבי יהודה follows the other opinion on that rule.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zekharya says:
This shows
phrases.notes: 'This' means רבי יהודה's own teaching about אוב and ידעוני from step 4.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehuda holds
two verses that come as one do teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲדָא אָמְרָה, קָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by naming רבי יהודה's view on the rule of parallel verses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Names the tanna's opinion: רבי יהודה holds the other side of a known dispute about parallel verses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone agrees that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד אין מלמדין, so רבי יהודה's לימוד looked impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds שני כתובים הבאים כאחד מלמדין, so learning all מכשפים from אוב and ידעוני is valid for him.

steps.title: Why sorcery is called כשפים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the word כשפים: it stands for 'they contradict the heavenly entourage.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: Why is sorcery called כשפים? Because it contradicts the heavenly entourage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a teaching about the name כשפים. רבי יוחנן explains what the word hints at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the word כשפים as a short form of the phrase מכחישין פמליא של מעלה. Sorcery seems to work against the order ה׳ set up through His heavenly entourage, and that is what its name says about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sorcery, witchcraft
They contradict / go against
The heavenly entourage (ה׳'s court of angels above)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
Why is their name called keshafim?
Because they contradict the heavenly entourage.
phrases.notes: He reads the word כשפים as a short form of the words מכחישין פמליא.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָן כְּשָׁפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the halachic discussion about the death penalty and starts aggadic teachings about sorcery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word כשפים means that sorcery goes against the order set up by ה׳'s heavenly entourage.

steps.title: Nothing besides ה׳, not even sorcery
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא teaches that the פסוק 'אין עוד מלבדו' includes sorcery: it has no power apart from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is none else besides Him.' רבי חנינא says: Even regarding sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק and gives רבי חנינא's reading of it. He says the פסוק also covers sorcery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says nothing has power besides ה׳‎. רבי חנינא adds that this is true even for sorcery. So sorcery cannot do anything against ה׳'s will.

keyTerms.meaning: There is none else besides Him (דברים 4:35)
Even
Regarding the matter of

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the story that comes next, where רבי חנינא shows he is not afraid of sorcery.

phrases.english: "There is none else besides Him"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:35

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says:
Even regarding sorcery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין עוֹד מִלְבַדּוֹ, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teachings about sorcery with a teaching about its limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'אין עוד מלבדו' includes sorcery: it has no power apart from ה׳.

steps.title: רבי חנינא is not afraid of a sorceress
steps.stepSummary: A woman tried to take dust from under רבי חנינא's feet to use for sorcery. He told her to go ahead if she could, since 'אין עוד מלבדו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain woman who was trying to take dust from under רבי חנינא's feet. He said to her: If you succeed, go do it. It is written: 'There is none else besides Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי חנינא. It shows him acting on his own teaching from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman wanted the dust to do sorcery against him. רבי חנינא was not worried, because he trusted the פסוק that nothing has power besides ה׳. The story shows how firmly he held his teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
Was trying / going around to
Dust
You succeed (literally, you are helped)
Go, do it

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי חנינא, 'אין עוד מלבדו' means sorcery cannot harm a person against ה׳'s will, and he lived by that.

phrases.english: There was a certain woman
who was trying
to take dust
from under the feet of Rabbi Chanina.
He said to her:
If you succeed,
go do it.
"There is none else besides Him" is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲוָת קָא מְהַדְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing רבי חנינא's teaching from step 8 in action.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's teaching that 'אין עוד מלבדו' applies even to sorcery.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the woman who tried to take dust from under his feet, and his calm answer quoting the פסוק.

steps.title: If sorcery has no power, why does it contradict Heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's fearless attitude using רבי יוחנן's teaching that מכשפים contradict the heavenly entourage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי יוחנן said: Why are they called מכשפים? Because they contradict the heavenly entourage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי חנינא's story. רבי יוחנן's teaching suggests sorcery has real power, so why wasn't רבי חנינא afraid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said מכשפים 'contradict the heavenly entourage,' which means sorcery can actually change what Heaven arranged. That clashes with step 9, where רבי חנינא acted as if sorcery could not hurt him at all. The גמרא sets the two side by side to show the tension.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?' A word that opens a challenge
'But didn't he say...?' It brings a source to challenge what was just said
The heavenly entourage, the angels and powers above

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Why are they called mekhashfim (sorcerers)?
Because they contradict the heavenly entourage.
phrases.notes: This is the same teaching we saw in step 7. Now the גמרא uses it to challenge the רבי חנינא story.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in step 9 using the teaching in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's claim that sorcery has no power over him (step 9)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מכשפים can contradict Heaven's plan, sorcery has real power, so רבי חנינא should have been careful.

steps.title: רבי חנינא was protected by his great merit
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא is a special case, because his great merit protected him from sorcery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא is different, because his merit was very great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Sorcery does have power, but not over someone as righteous as רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that sorcery works in general. It makes רבי חנינא an exception: his זכות shielded him. So רבי יוחנן's teaching still holds for ordinary people.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is different.' Used to set apart a special case
His merit
Is great / abundant

steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that anyone can ignore sorcery the way רבי חנינא did. The גמרא says he was an exception because of his great merit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina is different,
since his merit is great.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא, דִּנְפִישׁ זְכוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: רבי חנינא was a special exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי חנינא's story proves sorcery has no power at all
steps.terutzMaskana: Sorcery generally has power, but a person of very great merit is protected from it

steps.title: Two words for magic: demon-work and sorcery
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא explains that בלטיהם means demon-work and בלהטיהם means sorcery, and brings support from the flaming sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אייבו בר נגרי said in the name of רבי חייא בר אבא: 'בלטיהם' refers to acts done with demons. 'בלהטיהם' refers to acts of sorcery. And so too the פסוק says: 'and the flaming (להט) sword that turned every way.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. The Torah uses two similar words for what Pharaoh's magicians did, and the גמרא says each word describes a different kind of magic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלטיהם comes from the idea of something hidden, so it refers to demons, who work unseen. בלהטיהם refers to sorcery the sorcerer does himself. The flaming sword that turned by itself shows that להט describes something moving on its own through a power.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With their secret arts.' Here it means acts done with demons
'With their flames / enchantments.' Here it means acts of sorcery
Demons
'And so it says.' It brings a supporting פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Aivu bar Nagri said
that Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said:
"With their secret arts": these are acts of demons,
phrases.notes: שמות 7:22. The word sounds like 'hidden,' because demons work unseen.

phrases.english: "With their enchantments": these are acts of sorcery.
phrases.notes: שמות 7:11

phrases.english: And so it says:
"And the flaming sword that turned every way."
phrases.notes: בראשית 3:24. The sword turned on its own, like sorcery that works without demons.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ בַּר נַגָּרֵי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about kinds of magic, after the רבי חנינא discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בלטיהם means demon-work and בלהטיהם means sorcery, as shown by the flaming sword

steps.title: How to tell demon-work from sorcery
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a sign: if the magician insists on a specific tool, it is a demon; if not, it is sorcery.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If he is particular about which tool he uses, it is a demon. If he is not particular about the tool, it is sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a practical test to the previous teaching, so we can tell which of the two kinds of magic is being done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 named two kinds of magic. Here אביי says how to recognize them in real life: demon-work needs one exact tool, while sorcery works with any tool.

keyTerms.meaning: Is particular / insists
A utensil or tool

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One who is particular about the utensil: it is a demon,
phrases.notes: He means the magician insists on one specific tool for his magic.

phrases.english: one who is not particular about the utensil: it is sorcery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דְּקָפֵיד אַמָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 12 by giving a practical way to tell the two kinds of magic apart
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Insisting on a particular tool means demon-work; not insisting means sorcery

steps.title: Sorcery laws work like Shabbat laws: three levels
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches that like שבת, some sorcery gets סקילה, some is פטור אבל אסור, and some is מותר לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The laws of sorcery are like the laws of שבת. Some of them are punished with stoning, some are exempt from punishment but forbidden, and some are permitted from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a general framework with three levels of sorcery. This sets up the next part of the גמרא, which will give examples of each level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as on שבת some acts carry סקילה, some are only rabbinically forbidden, and some are fully allowed, sorcery has the same three levels. So not every magical-looking act gets the death penalty. Some are only forbidden, and some are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by stoning
Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden
Permitted from the outset

steps.whatToRemember: Sorcery has three levels like שבת: סקילה, פטור אבל אסור, and מותר לכתחילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This framework shapes the practical halacha. The punishment of מכשף applies only to the most severe level, not to every act that looks like magic.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The laws of sorcery are like the laws of Shabbat:
there are some of them punished by stoning,
and there are some of them that are exempt but forbidden,
and there are some of them that are permitted from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הִלְכוֹת כְּשָׁפִים כְּהִלְכוֹת שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new halachic statement by אביי that moves from kinds of magic to levels of punishment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sorcery acts fall into three levels like שבת: סקילה, פטור אבל אסור, and מותר לכתחילה

steps.title: Real magic gets stoning; fooling the eyes is exempt but forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains his first two levels: a real act of כישוף gets סקילה, and אחיזת עינים is פטור אבל אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who does a real magical act gets stoning. Someone who only fools people's eyes is not punished, but it is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the first two of אביי's three levels from Step 14. It tells us which kind of magic gets סקילה and which is only אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 gave the three levels in general terms; here they get definitions. If a person actually changes reality through magic, that is a real מעשה, so the punishment is סקילה. If he only creates an illusion so people think something happened, nothing real was done, so there is no punishment, but it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A real act; magic that actually changes something
Death by stoning
Literally 'grabbing the eyes'; an illusion that only fools what people see
Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden to do

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does not mean the act is allowed. It only means there is no court punishment. The act itself is still אסור.

phrases.english: One who performs a real act of magic is punished with stoning;

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹחֵז אֶת הָעֵינַיִם – פָּטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר.
phrases.english: one who only deceives the eyes is exempt from punishment, but it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה – בִּסְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first two of the three levels that אביי gave in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Real magic gets סקילה; illusion (אחיזת עינים) is פטור אבל אסור.

steps.title: The permitted level: creating a calf through the laws of creation
steps.stepSummary: The third level, מותר לכתחילה, is shown by רב חנינא and רב אושעיא, who created a calf every ערב שבת through הלכות יצירה and ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is fully allowed is like the case of רב חנינא and רב אושעיא. Every Friday they would study the laws of creation, a choice calf would be created for them, and they would eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third level of אביי's rule, which is fully allowed. It proves this with a story about two אמוראים who created a calf through holy study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This creation came from the holy wisdom of הלכות יצירה, the names and letters through which the world was made, not from impure forces. So it is not כישוף at all, and it is מותר לכתחילה. This finishes the comparison to שבת: some acts get סקילה, some are פטור אבל אסור, and some are completely permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted from the start, even ahead of time
ערב שבת; Friday
The laws of creation; holy wisdom about how the world was formed
A choice calf, either a third-born calf or one that reached a third of its growth

steps.whatToRemember: All three levels are now in place: real magic gets סקילה, illusion is פטור אבל אסור, and creation through holy wisdom is מותר לכתחילה.

phrases.english: What is permitted from the start
is like the case of רב חנינא and רב אושעיא:
Every Shabbat eve
they would study the laws of creation,
and a choice calf would be created for them,
phrases.notes: עִיגְלָא תִּילְתָּא means either a third-born calf or a calf a third grown. Either way, an especially good calf.

phrases.english: and they would eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּתָּר לְכַתְּחִלָּה – כִּדְרַב חֲנִינָא וְרַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's list by giving the third, fully permitted level.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creating through הלכות יצירה is not forbidden magic and is מותר לכתחילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It draws a clear line: an amazing result is not automatically forbidden. What matters is the power behind it.

steps.title: A magician pulls silk rolls from his nose
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that he saw קרנא's father blow his nose and throw rolls of silk out of his nostrils, which was a trick of the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I saw קרנא's father blow his nose and throw rolls of silk out of his nostrils.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells what he saw with his own eyes. It is a real-life example of the kind of trick that only fools the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No silk actually came out of the man's nose; it only looked that way. That makes it an example of אחיזת עינים, the middle level from Step 15, which is פטור אבל אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: I saw
He blew his nose; shook out
Rolls of silk

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
I saw the father of קרנא
blowing his nose and throwing out
rolls of silk from his nostrils.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: חֲזֵינָא לֵיהּ לַאֲבוּהּ דְּקַרְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of אחיזת עינים, the middle level from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A magician's trick of pulling silk from his nose was only an illusion.

steps.title: Demons cannot create anything smaller than a barley grain
steps.stepSummary: From the חרטומים saying 'אצבע אלהים היא' at the plague of lice, רבי אליעזר learns that a שד cannot create something smaller than a barley grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The magicians said to פרעה, 'This is the finger of God.' רבי אליעזר said: From here we learn that a demon cannot create a creature smaller than a barley grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about the magicians in מצרים, and רבי אליעזר learns a limit on what demons can do from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The magicians copied the earlier plagues, but at כנים (lice) they gave up and admitted it was from 'the finger of God.' רבי אליעזר explains why: lice are tiny, and the power of a שד cannot make anything smaller than a barley grain.

keyTerms.meaning: פרעה's magicians
The finger of God; something only God can do
A demon
The size of a barley grain

phrases.english: "And the magicians said to Pharaoh:
phrases.notes: שמות 8:15, at the plague of lice.

phrases.english: This is the finger of God."
רבי אליעזר said:
From here we learn that a demon is not able
to create a creature smaller than a barley grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: מִיכָּן שֶׁאֵין הַשֵּׁד יָכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the three levels of magic to a new question: what are the limits of a demon's power?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שד can create things, but nothing smaller than a barley grain.

steps.title: Demons cannot create at all; they only gather
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא swears that demons cannot create even something as big as a camel. They only gather large creatures from elsewhere and cannot gather tiny ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: By God! They cannot create even something the size of a camel. This kind (big animals) they can gather, and that kind (tiny ones) they cannot gather.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא disagrees with רבי אליעזר's idea that demons create things. He says they never create anything; they only bring together creatures that already exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר assumed demons really create things, just not tiny ones. רב פפא rejects that idea completely. The magicians' 'creatures' were real animals gathered from somewhere else. They failed at lice because tiny creatures cannot be gathered, not because demons can create only large things.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath: 'By God!'
A camel
Gathered together

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that demons can create, but not below barley size. רב פפא holds that demons cannot create at all; they can only gather large creatures, not tiny ones.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
By God!

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ כְּגַמְלָא נָמֵי לָא מָצֵי בָּרֵי.
phrases.english: Even something like a camel they cannot create either.
This kind can be gathered by them,
phrases.notes: 'This kind' means large creatures, which demons can bring from one place to another.

phrases.english: and that kind cannot be gathered by them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָאֱלֹהִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's idea that demons truly create, and explains the magicians' failure differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that a שד can create anything at all, even something large.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר assumed demons create things. In fact they only move creatures that already exist, and they cannot gather tiny ones like lice.

steps.title: רב saw an Arab slice up a camel and bring it back to life
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רבי חייא that he saw an Arab cut a camel apart with a sword, beat a drum, and the camel stood up again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רבי חייא: I saw it with my own eyes. A certain Arab took a sword and cut up a camel. Then he beat a drum, and the camel got up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב reports something amazing he saw: a camel cut apart and then brought back to life. This sets up רבי חייא's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing a dead animal back to life would seem to be real כישוף, the kind of act that gets סקילה. The question underneath is whether this was a real act or just a trick. The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: An Arab (a desert traveler)
A sword
A drum

phrases.english: Rav said to Rabbi Chiya:
I myself saw a certain Arab
who took a sword
and sliced up a camel,
and he beat on a drum, and it got up.
phrases.notes: 'It got up' means the camel stood up alive again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the stories about magic. It brings a case that looks like real כישוף, while step 17 was clearly a trick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב reports seeing a camel cut apart and seemingly brought back to life with a drumbeat.

steps.title: No blood or dung was left behind, so it was only a trick of the eyes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא asks whether blood and dung were left on the ground afterward. Since there were none, the act was only אחיזת עינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to him: After that, was there any blood or dung on the ground? Rather, since there wasn't, it was just a trick of the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רב. The camel was never really cut, so this was not real כישוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a camel were truly sliced open, blood and dung would spill out and stay on the ground. Nothing was left behind, so the cutting never really happened. The case moves from the 'real כישוף' level to the 'אחיזת עינים' level, which is פטור אבל אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Dung, the waste inside an animal's belly
A trick of the eyes; an illusion, not real magic

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא does not deny that רב saw it. He only shows that what רב saw was an illusion, not a real act.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical test for telling real כישוף (סקילה) apart from אחיזת עינים (פטור אבל אסור): does the act leave real physical results behind?

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לְבָתַר הָכִי, דָּם וּפַרְתָּא מִי הֲוַאי?
phrases.english: After that, was there blood and dung?
Rather, that was a trick of the eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר הָכִי, דָּם וּפַרְתָּא מִי הֲוַאי? אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea that the camel story in step 20 was real כישוף.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating the camel event as a real act of כישוף.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A real cutting would have left blood and dung behind. None was there, so it was only an illusion.

steps.title: זעירי's donkey turns into a bridge plank when it touches water
steps.stepSummary: זעירי buys a donkey in Alexandria. When he gives it water, the magic falls away and it turns into a bridge plank. The sellers refund him only out of respect, since everyone there tests purchases with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי came to Alexandria in מצרים and bought a donkey. When he went to give it water, the spell melted away and it turned into a plank from a bridge. The sellers said to him: If you weren't זעירי, we would not give you your money back. Does anyone here buy something without first testing it with water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another magic story, this time from מצרים, a place full of כישוף. Water breaks the spell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that in Alexandria, magic was so common that buyers routinely tested purchases with water to see if they were real. A buyer who skipped the test took the loss himself. זעירי got his money back only because he was a respected person.

keyTerms.meaning: Melted or thawed; here, the spell fell away
A plank of a bridge
We would give back (a refund)
Checks or tests

phrases.english: Ze'eiri happened to come
to Alexandria of Egypt.
He bought a donkey.
When he came to give it water to drink,
it melted away and became a bridge plank.
They said to him:
If you were not Ze'eiri,
we would not have given you back (your money).
Is there anyone who buys something here
and does not test it with water?

steps.triggerLanguage: זְעֵירִי אִיקְּלַע לַאֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִיָּא שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another magic story. This one shows a spell being broken by water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In Alexandria, buyers tested purchases with water because of magic. Someone who skipped the test took the loss, and זעירי was refunded only out of respect.

steps.title: ינאי turns the sorceress innkeeper into a donkey
steps.stepSummary: ינאי notices that the innkeeper bewitched his drink. He turns her own trick back on her and changes her into a donkey, until her friend breaks the spell in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: ינאי came to an inn and asked for water. They brought him a drink of flour mixed with water. He saw the woman's lips moving, so he spilled a little of it, and it turned into scorpions. He said: I drank from yours, now you drink from mine. He gave her a drink, and she turned into a donkey. He rode her to the market. Her friend came and broke the spell, and people saw him riding on a woman in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a third magic story. A sorceress tries to bewitch ינאי, and he turns the magic back against her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her moving lips told ינאי she was whispering a spell, and spilling some of the drink proved it. He paid her back in kind by turning her into a donkey. The ending shows the spell being undone by her friend, so he was left riding a woman in public.

keyTerms.meaning: An inn or lodging place
A drink of flour mixed with water
Her lips were moving (whispering a spell)
Scorpions

phrases.english: Yannai came to a certain inn.
He said to them: Give me water to drink.
They brought him a flour-and-water drink.
He saw that her lips were moving,
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the woman of the inn.

phrases.english: He threw out a little of it. It became scorpions.
He said to them: I drank from yours,
you too drink from mine.
He gave her to drink; she became a donkey.
He rode her and went up to the marketplace.
Her friend came and released her from the spell.
They saw him riding on a woman in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: יַנַּאי אִיקְּלַע לְהָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another magic story. Like step 22, it involves a donkey and a spell being undone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ינאי detected the innkeeper's spell and turned her into a donkey. Her friend later broke the spell in public.
steps.whatToRemember: The three stories in this section show magic in action: an illusion (the camel), a spell broken by water (זעירי's donkey), and a spell turned back on the sorceress (ינאי).

steps.title: The plague began with one frog that filled all of Egypt
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'ותעל הצפרדע', רבי אלעזר notes that 'frog' is singular. He explains that it was one frog that multiplied and filled the whole land of מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the frog came up and covered the land of מצרים.' רבי אלעזר said: It was one frog. It swarmed and filled the whole land of מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about the plague of frogs. רבי אלעזר explains why it says 'the frog' in the singular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the singular word הצפרדע, even though the land was full of frogs. רבי אלעזר reads this literally: the plague started with a single frog that multiplied. This opens a new piece connected to the plagues and the חרטומים discussed earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Frog (written in the singular in the פסוק)
It swarmed, multiplying into many

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אלעזר here with רבי אליעזר in step 18. They are two different sages with similar-looking names.

phrases.english: "And the frog came up
phrases.notes: שמות 8:2

phrases.english: and covered the land of Egypt."
Rabbi Elazar said:
It was one frog,
phrases.notes: He learns this from the פסוק saying 'the frog', in the singular.

phrases.english: it swarmed and filled the entire land of Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתַּעַל הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ וַתְּכַס אֶת אֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the magic stories and returns to the plagues of מצרים, the setting of step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plague of frogs began with one frog that multiplied and filled all of מצרים.

steps.title: This frog question is an older dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the single-frog idea is already a dispute between תנאים. It quotes רבי עקיבא, who says one frog filled all of מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. רבי עקיבא says: it was one frog, and it filled the whole land of מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links רבי אלעזר's teaching from the last step to an older argument between תנאים. It starts by quoting רבי עקיבא's side, and this sets up the other side in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כתנאי tells us there are two opinions about the singular word 'frog' in the פסוק. רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי אלעזר that one frog filled the whole land. The opposing view comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים (the sages of the משנה era)
Frog
The land of מצרים (Egypt)

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between Tannaim:
phrases.notes: The גמרא means that רבי אלעזר's idea from the last step is already argued about by earlier sages.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says,
it was one frog
and it filled the entire land of Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אלעזר's reading in step 24 matches one side of an older dispute between תנאים, the side of רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: the singular word 'frog' means one frog that filled all of מצרים.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rejects רבי עקיבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה tells רבי עקיבא to leave אגדה alone and focus on נגעים and אהלות. He then reads the פסוק as one frog that whistled to the others, and they all came.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to him: עקיבא, what are you doing with אגדה? Stop saying these things and go to נגעים and אהלות. It was one frog. It whistled to the others, and they came.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rejects רבי עקיבא's explanation. He gives his own explanation of why the פסוק says 'frog' in the singular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree the פסוק is talking about one special frog. They disagree about what that frog did. For רבי עקיבא, it multiplied into all the frogs. For רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, it only called the other frogs, so the many frogs were real separate frogs who came at its signal.

keyTerms.meaning: The non-legal parts of תורה learning: stories, lessons, and readings of פסוקים
The laws of צרעת impurity, a very complex area of הלכה
The laws of impurity spread by a dead body under a roof or tent, also very complex
She whistled (called out)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רבי אלעזר בן עזריה insulting רבי עקיבא's greatness. He is saying רבי עקיבא's real strength is the hardest areas of הלכה, not אגדה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said to him:
Akiva, what are you doing with aggada?
Stop with your statements
and go to Nega'im and Oholot.
It was one frog;
it whistled to them and they came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the dispute between תנאים that step 25 introduced. It rejects רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא's explanation that one frog multiplied to fill מצרים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The singular 'frog' does not have to mean one frog became all the frogs. It can mean one leading frog that called all the others.
steps.whatToRemember: The singular word 'frog' in ותעל הצפרדע has two explanations. In רבי עקיבא's view, one frog multiplied, which matches רבי אלעזר in step 24. In רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view, one frog whistled and all the others came.

steps.title: Back to רבי עקיבא's statement in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the opening words of רבי עקיבא's statement there, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said, and so on (as in the משנה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the frog discussion and goes back to the משנה. It quotes the start of רבי עקיבא's statement to set up a new discussion of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a setup line that opens a new section. The rest of רבי עקיבא's words are left out with כו׳, and the learner is expected to know them from the משנה. There, רבי עקיבא, in the name of רבי יהושע, says that of two people who gather cucumbers by sorcery, one is exempt and one is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for וְכוּלֵּיהּ, 'and so on'. The rest of the quote is not written out.
רבי עקיבא said: the opening words being quoted from the משנה
The base text the גמרא is explaining

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here. The rest is his teaching about two people who gather cucumbers by sorcery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the aggadic discussion of sorcery stories and the frog plague. Returns to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's statement of רבי עקיבא, which says some cucumber-gathering by sorcery is exempt and some is liable, as the starting point for the next discussion.
